questions.text:
An operating system uses the Banker's algorithm for deadlock avoidance when managing the allocation of three resource types X, Y, and Z to three processes P0, P1, and P2. The table given below presents the current system state. Here, the Allocation matrix shows the current number of resources of each type allocated to each process and the Max matrix shows the maximum number of resources of each type required by each process during its execution.

There are 3 units of type X, 2 units of type Y and 2 units of type Z still available. The system is currently in a safe state. Consider the following independent requests for additional resources in the current state:
REQ1: P0 requests 0 units of X, 0 units of Y and 2 units of Z
REQ2: P1 requests 2 units of x, 0 units of Y and 0 units of Z
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Need = Max [latex]-[/latex] Allocation: P0 (8,4,2), P1 (3,0,0), P2 (1,2,2). Available (3,2,2).
- REQ1 (P0 takes 0,0,2): available (3,2,0). P1 can finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (6,4,0), but then neither P0 (needs X = 8) nor P2 (needs Z = 2) can [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] unsafe, deny.
- REQ2 (P1 takes 2,0,0): available (1,2,2), P1 needs (1,0,0) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (6,4,2); P2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (8,5,3); P0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] safe, grant.

Answer: Only REQ2 can be permitted

options: Both REQ1 and REQ2 can be permitted
Neither REQ1 nor REQ2 can be permitted

questions.text:
Consider the following set of processes that need to be scheduled on a single CPU. All the times are given in milliseconds

Using the shortest remaining time first scheduling algorithm, the average process turnaround time (in msec) is ________.
questions.solution:
SRTF: A 0-3, B 3-5, A 5-8, C 8-12, E 12-15, D 15-21.
Turnaround: A 8, B 2, C 7, D 14, E 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average = 36 / 5 = 7.2 ms

Answer: 7.2

questions.text:
Assume that there are 3 page frames which are initially empty. If the page reference string 1,
2, 3, 4, 2, 1, 5, 3, 2, 4, 6, the number of page faults using the optimal replacement policy is
______
questions.solution:
Optimal (evict the page used furthest in the future), 3 frames:
1 F, 2 F, 3 F, 4 F (evict 3), 2, 1, 5 F (evict 1), 3 F (evict 5), 2, 4, 6 F

Faults = 7

Answer: 7

questions.text:
A canonical set of items is given below
S[latex]\rightarrow L. \gt R[/latex]
Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]R.
On input symbol [latex]\lt [/latex] the set has
questions.solution:
The item S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] L. [latex]\gt[/latex] R shifts only on "[latex]\gt[/latex]", so there is no shift on "[latex]\lt[/latex]". The set has just one complete item (Q [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R.), so there cannot be two reductions. No conflict on "[latex]\lt[/latex]".

Answer: neither a shift-reduce nor a reduce-reduce conflict

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: a shift-reduce conflict and a reduce-reduce conflict.
a shift-reduce conflict but not a reduce-reduce conflict
a reduce-reduce conflict but not a shift-reduce conflict.
neither a shift-reduce nor a reduce-reduce conflict

questions.text: Let L be a language and [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] be its complement. Which of the following is NOT a viable possibility?
questions.solution:
If both L and [latex]\bar L[/latex] are r.e., running their recognizers in parallel decides L, so L is recursive. "Both r.e. but not recursive" is therefore impossible; the other three cases do occur.

Answer: Both L and [latex]\bar L[/latex] are r.e. but not recursive

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Neither L nor [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] is recursively enumerable (r.e.).
One of L and [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] is r.e. but not recursive; the other is not r.e.
Both L and [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] are r.e. but not recursive
